items.title: 61427_Happy Caldwell oral history interview
items.q: Like this boy, Paul Quinichette Protege.

ctx.x: Yeah, because you got these classes. Like I did a jazz seminar over there where I worked, for City College, and I got to do one probably the end of the month. But I never would go into the full detail of theory and harmony and composition, like that, just on the chord basis and that when these fellows wonder, how did you do this with the chords. You can invert the chord, whatever you want to feel like, I said, because you got to hear it first, and then you use your own ideas. It's good to copy after

somebody else, I said, but it's best to try to get your own that can distinguish you from the other people, you know. I said, you can steal, I said, but you become prolific with it, if you do, then you're not doing nothing but like copy after Lester. Like this boy, Paul Quinichette Protege.
